inclusionReview.note: The action near James Island is individually included as a naval engagement, not the entire Pacific cruise. NHHC dates the captures of Catherine, Rose and Hector to 28 May 1813; Porter describes the captures and the armed resistance of Hector. Catherine and Rose did not resist, and Hector was encountered afterward. No precise offshore coordinate is established. The source date is retained; the later reunion with Essex on 24 June is not used as a battle date.

note: This ship-count comparison describes successive captures near James Island, not a simultaneous three-to-one gun battle. Only Hector fought. All three whalers were captured; Rose was then disarmed and released with the paroled prisoners, so removal denotes loss of fighting availability in this action, not permanent destruction or continued American possession. Georgiana survived and rejoined Essex. No human loss is inferred from captured ships. The May 28 date follows NHHC DANFS; Porter’s description is reported at the later reunion, not used to relocate or redate the action. Precise offshore location and specific whaler equipment remain unresolved. The action near James Island is individually included as a naval engagement, not the entire Pacific cruise. NHHC dates the captures of Catherine, Rose and Hector to 28 May 1813; Porter describes the captures and the armed resistance of Hector. Catherine and Rose did not resist, and Hector was encountered afterward. No precise offshore coordinate is established. The source date is retained; the later reunion with Essex on 24 June is not used as a battle date.
